subject: Odometer-style usage total — request for line-by-line breakdown
messages:
From: Emily Chen <billing@oxbridge.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: acct-ops@oxbridgehealth.com
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Odometer total on July invoice looks off

Hi Neha,

Hope you’re well — quick billing question about our July invoice (INV-OXB-0725). The total token count looks like an odometer jump at 23:59 UTC on July 31: the reported counter added ~18M tokens in one step even though our application had a quiet burstless window. Can you confirm how the platform attributes usage at billing boundaries? We rely on a continuous counter and need to reconcile to our internal telemetry.

Specifically we’d appreciate:
- a per-endpoint, per-model line-item for 2025-07-31 23:30:00 — 2025-08-01 00:30:00 UTC
- any session reassembly or post-processing rules that might attribute tokens retroactively
- whether prefix/KV caching evictions could cause re-counting on retries

We’ve attached a small extract from our side (session ids + timestamps) to help map events. Please let us know if you need a larger export. We’ve put the invoice on hold pending clarification.

Thanks,
Emily Chen
Billing Ops | Oxbridge Health
billing@oxbridge.com
+1 415-555-0182

[Attachment: session_samples.ndjson]

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <billing@oxbridge.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Odometer total on July invoice looks off

Thanks for the details, Emily — I’m on it. Short answer: we don’t (normally) retroactively re-attribute tokens, but there are a couple of cases where post-ingest aggregation or deduplication jobs can adjust counts (e.g., duplicate-request suppression, late-arriving batched events from older client SDK versions).

Next steps from our side: I’ll run a targeted export for the UTC window you called out and include per-endpoint and per-model counters, plus raw request ids. Ben — can you pull the 23:30–00:30 UTC slice of the usage counters and the platform’s deduplication job logs for that window? Marissa — please flag Finance that Oxbridge has the invoice on hold and we may be issuing a short investigation credit depending on findings.

I’ll follow up with the exports and an explanation within 48 hours. If you can send a compact mapping of your session ids → our request ids (or the session_samples.ndjson you attached), that will speed us up.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Emily Chen <billing@oxbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Odometer total on July invoice looks off

Neha / Emily — I pulled the exports. Summary:
- usage_counter_export_2025-07.csv attached contains per-shard counters, model name, route name, request_id, and timestamp (UTC).
- At 2025-07-31T23:59:12Z we have a burst where 17,842,913 additional tokens were recorded on shard-us-12, predominantly for model-redwood-7b-chat.
- The request_ids for that burst show a cluster of retries from the same client IP range followed by a late-arriving batch from an older SDK that sent events with timestamps ~2 minutes older than ingestion time. The dedupe job merged some duplicates but the late batch still contributed new token counts because the SDK re-sent full response payloads rather than delta summaries.

Why it looks like an odometer jump: our counters are monotonic per shard and the late batch was written shortly after ingestion into the same shard counter, so the visible counter increase is large even if the originating requests spanned a longer timeframe on the client side. We normally attribute by ingestion timestamp, not client timestamp, unless a customer requests otherwise for reconciliation.

I’m attaching the CSV and a short explanation of which request_ids we consider duplicates. Neha — I recommend offering a provisional credit for the overlapping duplicates while we work with the Oxbridge SDK team to update their client.

Attachments: usage_counter_export_2025-07.csv

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0133

From: Emily Chen <billing@oxbridge.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, acct-ops@oxbridgehealth.com
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Odometer total on July invoice looks off

Neha / Ben — thank you for the clear breakdown and for pulling the request-level evidence. The late-batch explanation matches what our infra team found: an outdated telemetry shim retried a bulk payload after a circuit-breaker event.

Requesting the following to close this out:
- a provisional credit for the duplicated tokens (we estimate ~11.2M tokens after you remove confirmed duplicates) applied to INV-OXB-0725, with a short note in the invoice line-item explaining the reason
- a brief recommended mitigation we can ship in our deploy (e.g., honor ingestion timestamp for reconciliation or provide an ingestion-window flag)

If you can confirm the credit and a one-paragraph mitigation doc by end of day Monday, we’ll release the invoice hold and process payment. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Emily Chen
Billing Ops | Oxbridge Health
[Attachment: session_samples.ndjson (original sample we sent)]
